headline: High: shared filesystem and broad tool/network access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can read/write application-defined files and has no self-isolation, while nullclaw reads/writes workspace files and supports browser, shell, and MCP tools. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path if the orchestrator passes outputs through files or tool outputs without provenance checks. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF the pair shares a workspace directory or file-backed handoff, injected instructions can cross from one agent to the other.
IF either agent treats file or tool output as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent in under 5 minutes.
Disable file-based handoff for untrusted content.
Add provenance tags to inter-agent messages.
Require explicit human approval before executing tool-derived instructions.
requires-engineering: add content filtering and instruction/data separation at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem read/write and network egress; nullclaw explicitly handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files, while LangGraph can touch graph state and developer-defined tools. If they share files or a common account, sensitive data can flow from one agent into the other's outputs or outbound requests. The blast radius includes secrets exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or state store, secrets may be exposed across the pair.
IF either agent forwards context to external model providers or APIs, leaked data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Use separate credentials and workspaces for each agent.
Redact secrets before any inter-agent transfer.
Restrict outbound network destinations for both agents.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after testing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, execute shells, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress; nullclaw also modifies git state and uses MCP. In a shared directory or repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. Because LangGraph has no self-isolation and nullclaw supports multiple channels, the conflict is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or repository, write-write conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking, concurrent shell or git actions can race.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories.
Disable git writes for one agent during shared runs.
Add a simple file lock around mutable resources.
Serialize shell actions that touch the same paths.
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is an orchestration framework that can pass its outputs into downstream nodes, and nullclaw exposes scheduling, delegation, and action-taking tools. If LangGraph-produced text is treated as authoritative by nullclaw, errors can cascade into emails, webhooks, or other external actions. The pair therefore has a default path from generated content to real-world side effects.
conditions: IF LangGraph output is fed into nullclaw without verification, mistakes can propagate.
IF nullclaw is configured to schedule or delegate based on upstream text, downstream actions may execute incorrect instructions.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before nullclaw acts on LangGraph output.
Require structured schemas for inter-agent messages.
Log and review all high-impact actions before execution.
Limit nullclaw to read-only mode for shared tasks.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and policy checks before action tools.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles touch sensitive operational data, but the profiles do not document a specific residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance risk is retention and handling of secrets, audit logs, and workspace files across two different systems with different storage models. Because the mismatch is plausible but not explicit, medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF the pair processes regulated data such as secrets or personal messages, retention and logging policies must align.
IF one system stores audit logs longer than the other, deletion/export obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Confirm both systems' retention settings in under 5 minutes.
Avoid regulated data in shared runs.
Disable verbose logging for sensitive sessions.
Document which system is the system of record.
requires-engineering: add policy mapping for residency, retention, and deletion workflows.
